caption: The drawing depicts a stone wall with a central arched doorway. The wall is composed of irregularly shaped, gray and beige stones, some of which display dark patches or weathered areas. Above the arched doorway is a barred window with vertical metal bars. Directly beneath the window, a skull and crossbones carving is visible, and two more skull and crossbones carvings are positioned symmetrically above either side of the door arch. The door itself is double-paneled and painted in a worn, light gray-blue color with visible wood grain. The archway surrounding the door is constructed from larger, rectangular tan stones with defined edges. Leading up to the doorway is a brick pathway or step, rendered in red and brown hues, with rectangular bricks set in rows. The overall composition is centered on the doorway, with the plain wall and brick pathway providing a frame of neutral tones.
title: Doorway and Door
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
